supply.firm_mw_source: Estimated from EIA actuals: Sept 6 2022 actual demand minus solar minus wind at the peak hour, plus a tuned cushion so the no-action evening is RED and the day needs the public alert to go green (demo calibration, not a measured firm-capacity figure). See docs/sources.md.

battery.note: ASSUMPTION: batteries assumed charged from midday solar. No recharge modeled.

sources.margin_target_pct: ASSUMPTION: 6% operating reserve margin target, in line with NERC-style minimums.
sources.supply.firm_mw: Estimated from EIA actuals: Sept 6 2022 actual demand minus solar minus wind at the peak hour, plus a tuned cushion so the no-action evening is RED and the day needs the public alert to go green (demo calibration, not a measured firm-capacity figure). See docs/sources.md.
sources.supply.solar_mw_by_hour: EIA CAISO hourly generation by fuel type (SUN), local hours, floored at 0.
sources.supply.wind_mw_by_hour: EIA CAISO hourly generation by fuel type (WND), local hours, floored at 0.
sources.battery.power_mw: E Source: CAISO had more than 3,900 MW of batteries, Sept 2022.
sources.battery.energy_mwh: ASSUMPTION: typical 4-hour batteries (3,900 MW x 4 h = 15,600 MWh).
sources.battery.start_soc_pct: ASSUMPTION: batteries assumed ~90% charged from midday solar.
sources.battery.efficiency: ASSUMPTION: 85% round-trip/discharge efficiency for grid batteries.
sources.precool.max_shift_mw: ASSUMPTION: up to 1,000 MW of load shiftable via utility pre-cooling programs.
sources.precool.rebound_pct: ASSUMPTION: 30% of shifted load rebounds the hour after pre-cooling ends.
sources.demand_response[0].mw: ASSUMPTION: utility demand response programs worth ~1,200 MW.
sources.demand_response[1].mw: ASSUMPTION: emergency load reduction program worth ~500 MW.
sources.public_alert.reduction_mw.low: Cal Advocates: ~2,000 MW drop in 20-30 min (low end used conservatively, 1,000 MW).
sources.public_alert.reduction_mw.likely: Cal Advocates: ~2,000 MW demand drop after the Sept 6 2022 text alert.
sources.public_alert.reduction_mw.high: E Source: up to ~2,400 MW reduction attributed to the alert.
sources.public_alert.max_hours: ASSUMPTION: a public alert runs at most 3 hours.
sources.public_alert.alerts_left_this_season: ASSUMPTION: 3 public alerts remain this season.
